episode_title: Ep.213 - Leaving a Legacy, Not a Headache

real_qa.q: What are the main legal documents every retiree should have in place for estate planning?
real_qa.r: A will is the starting point for your estate plan and everyone needs one. Beyond that, powers of attorney are crucial for healthcare and financial decisions if you become incapacitated. Trusts can provide additional protection and structure, especially if you have complicated family situations or want to protect heirs from long-term care costs. The specific combination depends on your individual circumstances and should be determined with an estate attorney.

real_qa.q: What is the difference between a revocable trust and an irrevocable trust?
real_qa.r: A revocable trust gives you flexibility and allows you to put things in and withdraw from it at any time, such as for home repairs or travel, but it does not protect you from long-term care costs or Medicaid planning. An irrevocable trust is more restrictive and pretty much set, but it offers asset protection against nursing home depletion and can help with government assistance planning. An estate attorney can determine which is appropriate for your situation.

real_qa.q: Why does a will become public record and what are the consequences?
real_qa.r: When a will goes through probate court, it becomes public record because creditors and debtors need to be able to review it. This means loss of privacy regarding your final wishes and assets. If there are disputes or claims against the estate, the probate process can become lengthy and expensive, with attorney fees accumulating as the court resolves disputes between family members or other entities.

real_qa.q: What changed in 2019 regarding inheritance taxes and required distributions?
real_qa.r: In 2019, the law changed for inheriting assets and for required minimum distributions from qualified accounts. For most retired clients, once they reach age 73, they are required to start taking money out of their IRA or 401k and pay taxes on it. This requirement is stretched over their entire lifetime, unlike prior to 2019.

real_qa.q: What percentage of clients lack basic estate planning documents when first consulting?
real_qa.r: Approximately 80% of clients who first come in do not have a will or trust. Many people postpone estate planning even into their 70s or 80s because they view it as important but not urgent. Randy recommends reviewing estate documents every 10 years since circumstances change, such as births, deaths, adoptions, or family situations.
